proxy_language: Proto-Semitic (with Proto-Afroasiatic as deeper backdrop); Biblical Hebrew/Akkadian/Arabic as reflex attestation sources
proxy_rationale: The Harifian (c. 10,500-9,500 BCE, Epipalaeolithic of the Negev and Sinai, a late Natufian-related culture) left no language. Its geographic and cultural position within the Levantine/Natufian sphere makes an early Afroasiatic/Semitic-adjacent language a defensible but unproven stand-in, since Natufians are often linked by some scholars (e.g. Bomhard, Militarev) to Proto-Afroasiatic or its Semitic branch. Proto-Semitic itself is dated roughly 4th-3rd millennium BCE, 6000+ years later, so the link is very weak. Reconstructed Proto-Semitic roots are used as stylistic models only, with no claim that Harifian people spoke them.
phonology: Proto-Semitic consonants (Kogan/Huehnergard): stops p b t d k g q with emphatic series (t' k' s'); fricatives s z sh (affricate-like lateral sh/s'); interdentals th dh and emphatic th'; velar/uvular x gh; pharyngeals h' and '; glottal h and glottal stop; sonorants m n l r w y. Vowels: a i u with length (aa ii uu), plus diphthongs aw ay. Root-and-pattern system with 3 consonantal radicals.
phonotactics: Syllables: CV, CVC, CVV; no initial vowels (initial glottal stop implied), no initial clusters in Proto-Semitic, no vowel hiatus. Stems are triconsonantal (some biconsonantal or quadriliteral). Word-final consonants allowed, nominative/genitive/accusative case vowels -u/-i/-a historically on nouns. Gemination of middle radical common in intensive/derived forms.
orthography: Use simplified scholarly Semitic transliteration without diacritics: ' for glottal stop, ` for pharyngeal ayin (written as ' or omitted), h for h and h-dot (merged), kh for velar fricative, gh for voiced velar/uvular, sh for shin, th and dh for interdentals, q for uvular stop, emphatics written as t', s', k'. Long vowels written as doubled vowels (aa, ii, uu). Avoid p/b clusters not attested.
morphology: Root-and-pattern: 3-consonant roots interleaved with vowel templates (e.g., qatal, qatil, maqtal, qattal). Prefixes: ma- (place/instrument), ta- (abstract/feminine nominal), sha- (causative). Suffixes: -at (feminine/abstract), -an/-aan (collective, intensifier), -iy (relational adjective). Nouns have gender (masc/fem), number (sg/dual/pl), and case endings in Proto-Semitic. Reduplication used in intensive/diminutive formations.
compounding: True compounding is rare; Semitic prefers the construct state (genitive chain): head noun first, followed by the genitive noun (e.g., bayt-X 'house of X', 'abd-X 'servant of X', bin-X 'son of X'). Agentive names use the active participle pattern (qaatil) or occupational pattern (qattaal). Place-instrument nouns use ma-qtal. Adjectives follow the noun and agree in gender/number.
noun_phrase_order: Head noun first, then genitive noun (construct state), then adjectives agreeing with the head; demonstratives usually follow. Pattern: N1-(N2 genitive) (ADJ).

attested_roots.gloss: water (cf. Akk. mu, Heb. mayim, Ar. ma')

worked_examples.name: mat'han
worked_examples.gloss: ma- (place prefix) + t'hn 'grind' root, pattern maqtal

notes: No word may be identical to a Modern Irish, Scottish Gaelic or Manx word. The Harifian language is wholly unknown; Proto-Semitic is used only as a flavor proxy and was spoken millennia later. Existing game names (Ghizagho, Cuc'oc, Hlathoshi) do not follow Semitic phonotactics; replace with triconsonantal root-based forms and construct-state genitives. Treat all output as invented fiction in a Semitic idiom, not as Harifian.
